caption: What if gravity stopped squashing you? It already does, every single day. You're about 1 to 2 cm taller when you wake up than you are at night. The reason is in your spine: between its bones sit 23 squishy discs, packed with a water-rich gel. While you stand, walk and sit, gravity slowly squeezes fluid out of them, so by evening you're around 1 cm shorter. Same you, same day! Lie down to sleep and the discs soak it back up, so you wake up tall again. Take gravity away completely and astronauts can grow up to 3% taller, about 5 cm for a 1.8 m person. The catch: most astronauts report back pain in space, and they shrink back to normal within a few months of coming home. Plot twist: the tallest you'll be all day is the moment you get out of bed. So if you ever need to measure your height, do it first thing in the morning. Morning or night: when are YOU tallest? 👇
